Lossless engineering vs zh-Hans listing copy — two different jobs

Teams assume lossless playback or ALAC support in the binary covers storefront language. iOS, macOS, MusicKit, and Connect actually separate hi-fi playback behavior from product-page copy:

  • ALAC decoding & lossless streaming pipelines — AVAudioEngine, MusicKit catalog bit-rate detection, and hi-fi playback routing in your app. Controls whether lossless tracks play — not App Store language. AppLocale does not implement this.
  • Settings → Music → Audio Quality — system Lossless and Hi-Res Lossless toggles on the buyer's device. Your listing may show these settings; wiring playback quality handlers is engineering, not listing copy.
  • In-app hi-fi badges & bit-rate UI — Lossless labels on Now Playing, quality tier pickers, and ALAC format indicators on your screens. Listing copy markets those surfaces on the product page; runtime player code is separate.
  • Pricing and Availability → China — makes the app downloadable on the China App Store. Separate from language rows.
  • App Store tab → Chinese (Simplified) localization — independent row for title, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text, screenshots, and caption lines. Empty or English here means China buyers see English fallback regardless of lossless features in the binary.

Working Lossless playback in the build and a localized China listing are both required when you sell on the China storefront — neither replaces the other. AppLocale covers how you describe Lossless, Hi-Res Lossless, ALAC, and Audio Quality on the product page in zh-Hans, not how you implement ALAC decoding or MusicKit catalog queries.

Lossless-specific listing vocabulary — what translates differently

Lossless marketing on App Store pages uses vocabulary general Music or Spatial Audio guides rarely cover. zh-Hans copy should reflect how Chinese buyers describe hi-fi playback workflows — not a literal paste of US marketing:

无损音频 vs 高解析度无损 vs ALAC

US pages use "Lossless", "Hi-Res Lossless", or "ALAC." China storefront copy often uses 无损音频 for standard Lossless tier badges, 高解析度无损 when gallery frames show Hi-Res Lossless or higher sample-rate callouts, and ALAC when your English listing names the codec explicitly. AppLocale aligns phrasing with each screenshot frame — not one blanket term for every overlay.

Lossless vs Spatial Audio vs Dolby Atmos

Lossless (无损音频) describes bit-rate and ALAC format quality — not surround channel positioning. Spatial Audio (空间音频) and Dolby Atmos (杜比全景声) describe immersive head-tracked sound — a different buyer story on the Spatial Audio guide. When your frame shows a Lossless badge on Now Playing, caption lines use 无损音频 — not 空间音频 unless the frame shows immersive sound UI.

Audio Quality settings vs in-app player chrome

Settings → Music → Audio Quality → Lossless is a system settings path — 设置 → 音乐 → 音频质量 → 无损. In-app quality tier pickers on your player screens need frame-matched captions — not generic Music hub vocabulary like 歌单 unless the screenshot shows a playlist.

Hi-Res Lossless vs standard Lossless

Standard Lossless covers up to 24-bit / 48 kHz ALAC. Hi-Res Lossless covers higher sample rates up to 24-bit / 192 kHz when catalog and hardware support it. zh-Hans copy should not promise 高解析度无损 on frames that only show standard Lossless badges — match caption vocabulary to the tier your English source claims.

Lossless vs Music hub playlists and lyrics

Playlist rows, lyrics panels, and Apple Music Sing belong on the Apple Music hub guide — 歌单, 歌词. Lossless bit-rate badges on Now Playing belong here — 无损音频, 高解析度无损 — unless your gallery actually leads with playlist discovery rather than hi-fi quality.

Subtitle and keyword packing

The 30-character subtitle and 100-character keyword field need Lossless-relevant search terms Chinese buyers type — see Simplified Chinese keywords & subtitle for field mechanics. Terms like 无损音频, 高解析度无损, and 高保真 each signal different intent from 空间音频 spatial terms or 歌单 playlist terms.
